_comment: Per testing-spec §1.12: mutation-testing health check on this crypto-adjacent library. NOT in PR CI. Run via `npm run mutate` from this package directory; surfaces a Stryker HTML report at reports/mutation/mutation.html plus a machine-readable JSON report at reports/mutation/mutation.json. Threshold of 80% mutation score is a target, not a gate. Below 80% triggers a tracking issue.
_runtime_comment: MEASURED 2026-09-03 (WI-2142121, first run ever in this repo): 401 mutants, 54 initial tests, concurrency 4, on a 128-core box at loadavg ~102 -> 1 minute 25 seconds wall clock, score 76.31. This file previously asserted '~10-30 min' and used that to justify a quarterly-only cadence; that estimate was an order of magnitude high and had never been checked against a run. Re-measure before citing a runtime here.
reporters_comment: 'json' emits the mutation-testing-elements JSON report — the machine-readable form any downstream consumer (e.g. mutation spec-evidence binding) should parse, rather than scraping clear-text stdout.
testRunner_comment: Vitest's stryker plugin: runs the existing vitest config per mutant. No extra setup needed.
thresholds_comment: break:0 means Stryker never fails its run on score alone — surface, don't gate. low:70 turns the report yellow; high:90 turns it green.
incremental_comment: Stores mutant/test state in incrementalFile — PINNED above to Stryker's own default path so this comment states a fact the config sets, rather than describing behaviour and drifting from it. Subsequent runs only re-mutate changed files. NOTE: incremental state is NOT in .stryker-tmp; that directory is the per-run sandbox COPY of your source and is deleted on completion (cleanTempDir defaults true), which is why an earlier version of this comment pointed readers at a path that never exists after a run. 'changed files' here means changed relative to this stored state — NOT a git ref, so the repo's origin/main-behind-staging skew cannot affect the scope.
